newsitem.title: USA: NYS Silver asks if state can afford big bond sale.
newsitem.headline: NYS Silver asks if state can afford big bond sale.

text.p: New York State Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, Thursday questioned if the state could afford a $7.3 billion bond sale to pay for a partial state takeover of the Long Island Lighting Co.

Republican Gov George Pataki has proposed what would be the nation's biggest tax-exempt bond sale to buy assets from LILCO and Brooklyn Union Gas, which plan to merge. The bonds would be sold by the Long Island Power Authority, which the state created in 1986 to acquire LILCO.
The deal would cut electricity rates for Long Island residents, who now pay some of the highest rates in the nation, by about 20 percent, Pataki says.

"Seven-point-three billion in Long Island might be something that he (Pataki) ought to consider initially as being an excessive bond issue," said Silver, in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. The Assembly Speaker would have to agree to the deal for it to go ahead.

Silver also noted that the plan only benefits one area of the state, though as a whole, its residents pay an average of 50 percent more for energy than people who live in other states. "It may be politically important to him (Pataki), that geographic region, but as part of the state, it is only a portion, and $7.3 billion of bonds is not the fiscal conservative's answer to a problem," said Silver.
Long Island is a Republican stronghold, and Pataki has built a reputation as a fiscal conservative.

Further, Silver said the deal might be too generous to LILCO's owners. "We are not asking LILCO or its stockholders to take any part of this hit, but the state of New York is shouldering the full burden of this deal."
The Assembly, which is holding hearings on the proposed deal, also plans to probe whether Long Island residents would capture the 20 percent rate cut the govenor forecasts.
